dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طِباقاً) the plural of طبقة, like رحبة and رحاب, or the plural of طبق, like جمل and جمال and جبل and جبال. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The origin of الطبق is a thing matching another thing in measure, covering it (muṭbiq) on all its sides».
(فُطُورٍ) cracks and fissures. In al-Mukhtār: «الفطر is splitting; one says فطره فانفطر, and تفطر الشيء means the thing cracked; its pattern is that of نصر».
(حَسِيرٌ) In al-Mukhtār: «حسر بصره means his sight was cut off from the length of the distance and the like, so it is حسير and also محسور; its pattern is that of جلس». It is of the pattern faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil (active participle), from الحسور, which is exhaustion.

* I'rab:
(تَبارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) تبارك is a past verb, meaning: He is exalted above the attributes of created beings; الذي is the fāʿil (agent); بيده is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الملك a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. هو is a mubtadaʾ, على كل شيء is attached (mutaʿalliq) to قدير, and قدير is the khabar of هو; this clause is conjoined to the ṣila, confirming its content. (الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَياةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا) الذي is a badal (substitute) for the first relative noun, and the clause خلق الموت والحياة has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. In ليبلوكم the lām is causal, and يبلو is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; its agent is "he" and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). أيّكم is a mubtadaʾ, أحسن the khabar, and عملا a tamyīz (specification); the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the second object of يبلوكم. The causal lām and its genitive are attached to خلق insofar as it relates to life, since life is the place of testing and obligation, whereas there is nothing of that in death. In the speech there is a dependent allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya tabaʿiyya), likening their state — in His (the Exalted's) imposing His obligations on them, creating death and life for them, rewarding and punishing them — to the state of one who tests someone he has tried and examined to see the extent of his obedience or disobedience, and then honours or humiliates him. (وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ) a mubtadaʾ and its two khabars. (الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقاً) الذي is a second badal for the relative noun; it is also said to be a badal for العزيز الغفور, and it is said to be a naʿt (adjective) for them both, or to be in the position of a nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or accusative by way of praise. The clause خلق is the ṣila, سبع سموات is a mafʿūl bihi, and طباقا is an adjective for سبع سموات, or accusative by an implied verb, i.e. طبقت طباقا, in which case it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of طابق: مطابقة and طباقا. (ما تَرى فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمنِ مِنْ تَفاوُتٍ فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرى مِنْ فُطُورٍ) resumptive speech, introduced to emphasise the soundness of His (the Exalted's) creation. ما is negating, ترى is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), referring to whoever is fit to be addressed; في خلق الرحمن is attached to ترى; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and تفاوت is genitive in form and accusative in position as the object of ترى. It was also read تفوّت, with a doubled wāw and no alif. التفاوت is lack of proportion, because some parts fall short of (يفوت) others. It is strange that al-Zamakhsharī made this clause an adjective following on from His words طباقا. He said:
«This negated clause is an adjective for His words طباقا. Its original form is ما ترى فيهنّ, and خلق الرحمن was put in place of the pronoun to magnify their creation and to draw attention to the cause of their soundness, which is that they are the creation of the All-Merciful.» This involves all the strain it does, since it detaches parts of the speech from one another.
فارجع: the fāʾ is causal, because His words فارجع البصر are caused by His words ما ترى. ارجع البصر is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi; هل is an interrogative particle, ترى an imperfect verb in the nominative, من a redundant preposition, and فطور genitive in form and accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi. The interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative by an omitted verb, and this verb is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, i.e. هل ترى. (ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنْقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ الْبَصَرُ خاسِئاً وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; ارجع البصر is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi; كرتين is accusative as a maṣdar, like مرتين; although it is a dual, the dual is not intended by it — rather multiplicity is intended. ينقلب is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it falls as the answer to the command; إليك is attached to ينقلب, البصر is the agent and خاسئا a ḥāl (circumstantial). The wāw is circumstantial, هو a mubtadaʾ and حسير the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl either from the owner of the first ḥāl or from the pronoun latent in the ḥāl before it, so that it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).

dervis-irab:5-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رُجُوماً) الرجوم is the plural of رجم, a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a name for the object, i.e. that with which one pelts. It may also remain a maṣdar, with a muḍāf implied, i.e. ذات رجوم (possessing pelting). The maṣdar was pluralised only with regard to its kinds.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِمَصابِيحَ وَجَعَلْناها رُجُوماً لِلشَّياطِينِ) resumptive speech, introduced to begin mentioning further proofs of the completeness of His (the Exalted's) power. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), زيّنا is a verb and its agent, السماء a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and الدنيا a naʿt (adjective), meaning the nearest to the earth; بمصابيح is attached (mutaʿalliq) to زيّنا. جعلناها is a verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi, رجوما a second object, and للشياطين is attached to رجوما or is an adjective for it. (وَأَعْتَدْنا لَهُمْ عَذابَ السَّعِيرِ) أعتدنا is conjoined to زيّنا, لهم is attached to أعتدنا, and عذاب السعير is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) the wāw is a conjunction, للذين is a fronted khabar (predicate), the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), بربهم is attached to كفروا, and عذاب جهنم is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). بئس المصير is a non-inflecting (jāmid) verb for the expression of blame, and its agent; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being هي. (إِذا أُلْقُوا فِيها سَمِعُوا لَها شَهِيقاً وَهِيَ تَفُورُ) إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to سمعوا; the clause ألقوا is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. ألقوا [Translator's note: the source prints «و. لقوا»] is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); فيها is attached to ألقوا, and the clause is resumptive. The clause سمعوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. لها is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from شهيقا, because it was originally its adjective and was placed before it; شهيقا is the object of سمعوا. The wāw is circumstantial, هي a mubtadaʾ and the clause تفور its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in لها. (تَكادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ كُلَّما أُلْقِيَ فِيها فَوْجٌ سَأَلَهُمْ خَزَنَتُها أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَذِيرٌ) The clause is resumptive, as if it came as the answer to a questioner's question. تكاد is an imperfect verb from the verbs of approximation; its subject is latent (mustatir), implied as هي, and the clause تميّز is its khabar. تميّز is originally تتميّز, an imperfect verb meaning "is torn apart", and one of the two tāʾs was dropped. من الغيظ is in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification), i.e. غيظا. كلما is an adverb of time attached to its answer, which is سألهم; the detailed i'rab of it has already been given. ألقي is a passive past verb, فيها is attached to ألقي, and فوج is the nāʾib fāʿil. The clause سألهم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; it is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi, and خزنتها is the agent. The hamza is for the interrogative of confirmation and rebuke; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive, يأتكم is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم, the kāf a mafʿūl bihi, and نذير the agent. The interrogative clause is the second object of سأل. (قالُوا بَلى قَدْ جاءَنا نَذِيرٌ) قالوا is a verb and its agent, قد a particle of affirmation, جاءنا a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and نذير a postponed agent. The clause is resumptive, answering an implied question, as if it were said: "So what did they say after the question?", and He said: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير. The clause قد جاءنا is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). (فَكَذَّبْنا وَقُلْنا ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction, كذبنا a verb and its agent, and قلنا is conjoined to كذبنا. ما is negating, نزل a past verb, الله the agent, من a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and شيء genitive in form and accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. (إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ كَبِيرٍ) إن is negating, أنتم a mubtadaʾ, إلا a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), في ضلال the khabar of أنتم, and كبير a naʿt. (وَقالُوا لَوْ كُنَّا نَسْمَعُ أَوْ نَعْقِلُ ما كُنَّا فِي أَصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ) the wāw is a conjunction, قالوا a past verb and its agent; لو is conditional; كان and its subject, and the clause نسمع is its khabar; أو is a conjunction and نعقل is conjoined to نسمع. ما is negating; كان and its subject, and في أصحاب السعير is its khabar; the clause has no grammatical position, and the conditional clause with its apodosis is the maqūl al-qawl. (فَاعْتَرَفُوا بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسُحْقاً لِأَصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, اعترفوا a verb and its agent, and بذنبهم is attached to اعترفوا. The fāʾ is a conjunction and سحقا is accusative as a maṣdar, its implied form being سحقهم الله سحقا; the maṣdar stood in for its governing verb in an imprecation, like جدعا له and عقرا, so it is not permissible to make it overt. It is also said to be a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, i.e. ألزمهم الله سحقا. In al-Mukhtār:
«السحق is remoteness; one says سحقا له, and السحق with two ḍammas is the same. سحق الشيء, with a ḍamma, سحقا on the measure of بعد, so it is سحيق, i.e. remote; and أسحقه الله means Allah removed him far away.» The regular form would have been إسحاقا, but the maṣdar was brought according to the omitted (verb). The lām in لأصحاب السعير is for clarification (bayān), as in هيت لك.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «ولقد زيّنا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He likened the planets and stars to lamps, omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it is likened to, by way of an original explicit metaphor, because people adorn their mosques and houses by lighting lamps — but these are lamps whose brightness your lamps cannot match.
2- In His words «تكاد تميز من الغيظ» there is a dependent implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya): He likened Hell to a woman enraged at them, because of the intensity of its boiling with them, omitted the thing it is likened to and kept something of its concomitants, because an enraged woman is torn apart and splits with anger, and her parts almost separate from one another because of the intensity of her agitation; people say "So-and-so is torn apart with rage" when they describe him as excessive in anger. In this verse there is also the device of "fine following" (ḥusn al-ittibāʿ), for the poets have followed its path and become fond of attributing the actions of rational beings to what is not rational. We have given examples of it in al-Kahf and in al-Furqān, so refresh your acquaintance with them.

dervis-irab:12-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ذَلُولًا) faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), i.e. made submissive, subjugated, compliant with what you want of it.
(مَناكِبِها) المناكب is the plural of منكب, which is where the top of the shoulder-blade meets the upper arm. One says: "the shoulders and heads among them were alike", i.e. none of them is preferred over another; one says: "he shook his shoulder at such-and-such", i.e. he rejoiced at it; and "so-and-so is with me on the edge of a shoulder", i.e. whenever he sees me he turns away and does not meet me with his face. المنكب is also the side and flank of anything; one says: "we travelled in a منكب of the land or of the mountain", i.e. in a side of it. The منكب of a people is their chief or their helper, and the منكب of the land is the road and the raised place. In the Noble Quran: «فامشوا في مناكبها», i.e. in its elevated places; on this basis the speech is literal, while on the first sense there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya) in it. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: «Walking on its shoulders is a similitude for the excess of subjugation and its passing the limit, because the two shoulders and the place where they meet at the withers are the most delicate part of the camel and the least suited to the rider treading on it with his foot and resting his weight on it. So when He made it so submissive that one walks on its shoulders, He left nothing of it that He had not made submissive.» Al-Zajjāj said: «Its meaning is: He made travelling in its mountains easy for you; and if travelling in its mountains is possible for you, that is more eloquent in expressing subjugation.» It is also said: its sides.
(تَمُورُ) it moves with you. In al-Mukhtār: «مار, of the pattern of قال, means it moved and came and went; from it: يوم تمور السماء مورا. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it surges in waves.»

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ) إنّ and its subject; the clause يخشون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; ربهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالغيب is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in يخشون, the bāʾ being in the sense of في. لهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and مغفرة a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); أجر is conjoined to مغفرة and كبير is a naʿt (adjective) for أجر; the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ. (وَأَسِرُّوا قَوْلَكُمْ أَوِ اجْهَرُوا بِهِ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ) the wāw is resumptive; أسرّوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; قولكم is a mafʿūl bihi; أو is a conjunction; اجهروا is an imperative verb and its agent, and به is attached (mutaʿalliq) to اجهروا. إنّ and its subject, عليم its khabar, and بذات الصدور is attached to عليم. The clause of إنّ and what falls within its scope gives the reason for the command: that secret and open are equal with respect to His (the Exalted's) knowledge. (أَلا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ) the hamza is interrogative, لا negating, and يعلم an imperfect verb in the nominative; من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah the Exalted. The meaning is: is His knowledge of those He created to be negated, when He is the One who encompasses the hidden and the manifest aspects of things? Al-Zamakhsharī permitted — and al-Jamal in his Ḥāshiya preferred it, quoting from his teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ [Translator's note: the source prints «أبو البقاء» in the nominative here], and others — that من be the agent of يعلم with the object omitted, as if He said: does the Creator not know your secret and your open speech? The interrogative means disavowal (inkār). Al-Zamakhsharī's wording is: «It may be that من خلق is accusative, in the sense: does He not know what He created, when this is His state? It is related that the polytheists used to say things among themselves, and Allah would inform His Messenger of them, so they would say: "Keep your speech secret, lest the God of Muhammad hear it." So Allah drew attention to their ignorance. If you say: you have implied an object for ألا يعلم, in the sense "does the one who created not know that which was mentioned — what is concealed in the heart and expressed with the tongue?" — so why did you not make it like their saying "he gives and withholds", and why is the meaning not "is the one who is a creator not knowing?", since creating is valid only with knowledge? I say: the ḥāl, which is His words وهو اللطيف الخبير, refuses that, because if you said "is the one who is a creator not knowing, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?", it would not be a sound meaning, because ألا يعلم leans on the ḥāl, and a thing is not timed by itself; one does not say "does he not know, while he is knowing?", but rather "does he not know such-and-such, while he is knowing of everything?"» Ibn al-Munayyir al-Mālikī followed up al-Zamakhsharī and debated him in a valuable discussion, in which he said: «This verse is a refutation of the Muʿtazila and a validation of the path the people of the Sunna take in refuting them. For the people of the Sunna argue that the servant does not create his actions on the grounds that he does not know them, and this is an inference from the negation of the concomitant — knowledge — to the negation of what entails it — creation. The verse points to this very entailment, for Allah the Exalted guided to inferring the establishment of knowledge for Him, Mighty and Majestic, from the establishment of creation, which is an inference from the existence of what entails to the existence of the concomitant. So it is a single light from which one draws both the establishment of knowledge for the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, and the invalidation of the servant's creating his actions. The i'rab of the verse comes down to this meaning: the correct approach in it is that من is the agent, meaning the Creator, and the object of the knowing is omitted, its implied form being ذلك, referring to the secret and the open, and the object of خلق is omitted, its pronoun referring to ذلك. The implied form in all of it is: does the one who created the secret and the open not know them? Whenever we follow any approach to the i'rab other than this, it throws us into the straits of strain and forcedness. It is possible that من is its object, applying to the doer of the secret and the open, the implied form being "does Allah not know those who keep secret and those who speak openly?" — but that does not match the detailed statement, for it did not fall upon the persons of the doers but upon their actions, namely the secret and the open, and it is upon this that the inference fell. Other possibilities, more remote than this, exist; the first is the more fitting in wording and meaning, and Allah is the One who grants success.» The wāw is circumstantial, هو a mubtadaʾ, اللطيف a first khabar and الخبير a second khabar. (هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ ذَلُولًا فَامْشُوا فِي مَناكِبِها وَكُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِهِ وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ) هو is a mubtadaʾ, الذي the khabar, and the clause جعل is the ṣila; لكم is attached to ذلولا; الأرض is the first object of جعل and ذلولا its second object if it is in the sense of "made into"; if it is in the sense of "created", it is parsed as a ḥāl. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied condition), i.e. "if you know that, then walk"; the command is one of permission. في مناكبها is attached to امشوا; كلوا is an imperative verb and its agent, and من رزقه is attached to كلوا. إليه is a fronted khabar and النشور a postponed mubtadaʾ. (أَأَمِنْتُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّماءِ أَنْ يَخْسِفَ بِكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فَإِذا هِيَ تَمُورُ) the hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal; أمنتم is a verb and its agent; من is a mafʿūl bihi, and it refers
to Allah the Exalted; في السماء is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun. أن يخسف: the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of an accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for «من»; بكم is attached to يخسف, and الأرض is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is a conjunction and إذا is the إذا of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya), which has been discussed before; هي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تمور the khabar. (أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّماءِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حاصِباً فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ كَيْفَ نَذِيرِ) أم is a conjunction in the sense of بل, as if He turned away from the first threat to move on to another threat; أمنتم is a verb and its agent, من a mafʿūl bihi, في السماء the ṣila; أن and what falls within its scope is a badal ishtimāl for «من», and حاصبا is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, the sīn is a particle of the future, and تعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn; كيف is an interrogative noun, a fronted khabar, and نذيري a postponed mubtadaʾ, the yāʾ of the first person having been dropped in writing; the suspended clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of تعلمون.

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطَّيْرِ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The plural of الطائر is طير, like صاحب and صحب and راكب and ركب, and the plural of الطير is طيور and أطيار. Abū ʿUbayda and Quṭrub said: الطير applies to the singular and the plural. Ibn al-Anbārī said: الطير is a collective, and treating it as feminine is more common than treating it as masculine; one does not call a single one طير but طائر, and rarely is the female called طائرة.» In al-Qāmūs, al-Lisān and others there is what may be summed up as: الطير is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and the plural of طائر; it may apply to a single one; and it is the noun from التطيّر (taking evil omens), from which comes their saying: "There is no omen but Allah's omen", and "Allah's omen, not your omen", just as one says: "Allah's morning, not your morning". One also says: "as if birds were on their heads", i.e. they are still out of awe; its origin is that the crow lands on the camel's head and picks ticks off it, so the camel does not move lest the crow fly away from it. And "restrain the sides of your bird", i.e. the sides of your levity and rashness.
(صافَّاتٍ) spreading their wings in the air when flying.
(وَيقبضنها) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is ﴿وَيَقْبِضْنَ﴾] and folding them in when they beat their sides with them. More will come in the section on rhetoric.
(لَجُّوا) they persisted.
(مُكِبًّا) an active participle from أكبّ, the intransitive verb that is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of كبّه. One says: "Allah threw him (كبّه) on his face into the Fire, فأكبّ", i.e. he fell. This goes against the rule that when the hamza enters an intransitive verb it makes it transitive; here it has entered the [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires "transitive"] verb and made it intransitive. This is what the lexicographers mention, and al-Zamakhsharī rejected it, saying: «They make أكبّ the reflexive of كبّه — one says كببته فأكبّ — as one of the rarities and anomalies, and similarly قشعت الريح السحاب فأقشع (the wind dispersed the clouds and they dispersed). It is not so, and nothing of the pattern afʿala is reflexive; only those who carry the Book of Sībawayh master this. Rather, أكبّ belongs to the category of أنغض and ألأم, and its meaning is: he entered into falling on the face and came to have it. Likewise أقشع السحاب: the clouds entered into dispersal. The reflexive of كبّ and قشع is انكبّ and انقشع.» In al-Ṣiḥāḥ there is what supports al-Zamakhsharī's statement. It says: «أنغض القوم: their wealth perished, and also انفضّوا, like أرملوا: their provisions ran out.» And in it also: «ألأم الرجل: when he does what makes people call him base (لئيم).»
Abū Ḥayyān said: «مكبّا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), from أكبّ, which is intransitive, while كبّ is transitive; the Exalted said: فكبت وجوههم في النار. The hamza in it is for entering into the thing or for becoming. The reflexive of كبّ is انكبّ: you say كببته فانكبّ.»
In al-Qāmūs: «كبّه: he overturned him and threw him down, like أكبّه and كبكبه, so he fell (فأكبّ); it is intransitive and transitive.»
The wording of al-Asās: «أكبّ لوجهه and على وجهه, فانكبّ: أفمن يمشي مكبّا على وجهه. كببته, and he is مكبوب and مكبوت. I threw him (كببته) into the pit, and كبكبته, likewise when he threw him from the top of a mountain or a wall. The horseman brings down (يكبّ) the wild beasts, and they bring down (slaughter) the pregnant she-camels. He said:
يكبّون العشار لمن أتاهم ... إذا لم تسكت المائة الوليدا
(They slaughter the pregnant she-camels for whoever comes to them, when even a hundred camels would not quieten the newborn child.)
And a man أكبّ is one who keeps stumbling. ʿAdī said:
إن يصبني بعض الهنات فلا وا ... ن ضعيف ولا أكبّ عثور
(If some misfortunes befall me, I am not a weak laggard, nor one who keeps stumbling and falling.)
Among the figurative uses: أكبّ على عمله — he devoted himself to his work — and he is مكبّ عليه, keeping to it and not leaving it. Labīd said:
جنوح الهالكي على يديه ... مكبّا يجتلي نقب النصال
(Like the smith bending over his hands, intent, polishing the rust-spots of the blades.)
And أكبّ فلان على فلان: he came at him, seeking him.»

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ) the wāw is resumptive, the lām introduces the oath (al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), قد is a particle of affirmation, كذب a past verb, الذين the agent, and من قبلهم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The fāʾ is a conjunction, كيف an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and نكير its subject, the yāʾ having been dropped following the script of the Muṣḥaf, i.e. my disapproval of them. (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهُمْ صافَّاتٍ وَيَقْبِضْنَ) the hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal, and the wāw conjoins to something implied, i.e. "were they heedless?"; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; يروا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم and the wāw is the agent; إلى الطير is attached to يروا; فوقهم is an adverb attached to صافّات, and صافّات is a ḥāl. ويقبضن: the wāw is a conjunction, and يقبضن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the agent. The secret of conjoining the imperfect verb to the derived noun will come in the section on rhetoric. The object of يقبض is omitted, i.e. their wings. (ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا الرَّحْمنُ إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ بَصِيرٌ) the clause is resumptive, or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of يقبضن. Abū al-Baqāʾ parsed it as a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in يقبضن, and I see no justification for this parsing. ما is negating, يمسكهنّ an imperfect verb in the nominative and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), إلا a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) and الرحمن the agent. إنّ and its subject; بكل شيء is attached to بصير, and بصير is the khabar of إنّ. The clause gives the reason for the power that brings everything within the range of its knowledge. (أَمَّنْ هذَا الَّذِي هُوَ جُنْدٌ لَكُمْ يَنْصُرُكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ الرَّحْمنِ) أم is a conjunction in the sense of بل, so it is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa); من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and هذا a demonstrative, the khabar; الذي is a badal for هذا or an adjective for the demonstrative; هو is a mubtadaʾ, جند the khabar, and لكم [Translator's note: the source prints «ولكن»] a naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. The clause ينصركم is a second naʿt or a ḥāl, and من دون الرحمن is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of ينصركم. (إِنِ الْكافِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ) إن is negating, الكافرون a mubtadaʾ, إلا a particle of restriction, and في غرور the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa) with no grammatical position. (أَمَّنْ هذَا الَّذِي يَرْزُقُكُمْ إِنْ أَمْسَكَ رِزْقَهُ) conjoined to what preceded. إن is conditional and أمسك a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what preceded; رزقه is a mafʿūl bihi. (بَلْ لَجُّوا فِي عُتُوٍّ وَنُفُورٍ) بل is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction, لجوا a past verb and its agent, في عتو is attached to لجوا, and نفور is conjoined to عتو. (أَفَمَنْ يَمْشِي مُكِبًّا عَلى وَجْهِهِ أَهْدى أَمَّنْ يَمْشِي سَوِيًّا عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) the hamza is for the interrogative of rebuke, and the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted and implied; من is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يمشي is the ṣila; مكبّا is a ḥāl from the agent of يمشي, and على وجهه is attached to مكبّا; أهدى is the khabar. أم is a conjunction balancing the interrogative hamza, and من is conjoined to the first من; the clause يمشي is the ṣila, سويا a ḥāl, and على صراط مستقيم is attached to يمشي.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «أو لم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافّات ويقبضن» the verb is conjoined to the noun, while the context requires saying قابضات. That is for a subtle secret: the basis of flight is the spreading of the wings, because flying in the air is like swimming in water, and the basis of swimming is stretching out and spreading the limbs. Folding, on the other hand, is something occasional that comes upon the spreading, to gain help from it in moving. So what is occasional and not basic was brought in the form of a verb, in the sense that they are spreading, and folding happens from them time after time, as it happens from the swimmer. In sum: spreading is predominant, so it is as if it were the fixed state, and it was expressed by the noun; folding recurs anew, so it was expressed by the verb.
2- In His words «أفمن يمشي مكبّا على وجهه أهدى أم من يمشي سويّا على صراط مستقيم» there is an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), and it is a similitude for the believer and the disbeliever. The disbeliever is blind, not guided to the road; rather he walks aimlessly, constantly stumbling and falling on his face. The believer has sound sight and walks on a clear, straight road, safe from stumbling and falling on his face. Thus the Quran's method of embodiment (tajsīd) becomes manifest.

dervis-irab:23-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زُلْفَةً) الزلفة: nearness.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَكُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ) هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject), الذي the khabar (predicate), and the clause أنشأكم the ṣila (relative clause); the nominal clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). جعل is conjoined to أنشأكم, and لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to جعل or is in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جعلنا [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has جعل]. The difference between جعل in the sense of creating and جعل in the sense of making into has been given before. السمع is a mafʿūl bihi, الأبصار is conjoined to السمع, and الأفئدة is also conjoined. قليلا is the adjective of a fronted maṣdar (verbal noun), ما is redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the paucity, and تشكرون is an imperfect verb in the nominative. قليلا may also be parsed as an adverb attached to تشكرون, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). (قُلْ هُوَ الَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ) هو is a mubtadaʾ, الذي its khabar, and the clause ذرأكم the ṣila; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. في الأرض is attached to ذرأكم, إليه is attached to تحشرون, and تحشرون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) the wāw is a conjunction; يقولون is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. متى is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, and the adverb is attached to an omitted element in the position of a nominative as a fronted khabar; هذا is a postponed mubtadaʾ and الوعد a badal (substitute). إن is conditional, and كنتم is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); كان and its subject, and صادقين its khabar. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "if you are truthful in what you report about the matter of the Resurrection and the Gathering, then make clear its time precisely". (قُلْ إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) إنما is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; العلم is a mubtadaʾ and عند الله an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. إنما is conjoined to the first إنما; أنا is a mubtadaʾ, نذير the khabar and مبين a naʿt (adjective). The two clauses are the maqūl al-qawl. (فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ زُلْفَةً سِيئَتْ وُجُوهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals implied clauses), because it expresses two implied clauses, as if it were said: "and what they were promised came to them and they saw it; so when they saw it". لمّا is temporal (ḥīniyya) or a linking particle containing the sense of a condition; رأوه is a past verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi; زلفة is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of رأوه; it is a noun of maṣdar from أزلف, in the sense of an active participle. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted parsing it as an adverb, i.e. a place possessing nearness. The clause سيئت has no grammatical position because it is the answer of لمّا; وجوه is the nāʾib fāʿil, الذين a muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause كفروا the ṣila. (وَقِيلَ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَدَّعُونَ) the wāw is a conjunction; قيل is a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir), i.e. the keepers said to them. هذا is a mubtadaʾ and الذي a relative noun in the position of a nominative as an adjective of the omitted khabar, i.e. "this is the punishment which"; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; كان and its subject, به is attached to تدعون, and the clause تدعون is the khabar of كنتم. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَهْلَكَنِيَ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ مَعِيَ أَوْ رَحِمَنا) أرأيتم: the hamza is for the interrogative of disavowal (inkār), and رأيتم, in the sense of "inform me", is a verb and its agent. إن is conditional, and أهلكني الله is a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi and an agent; the following conditional clause stands in place of the two objects of أرأيتم; parallels of this parsing have been given before. إن is conditional and أهلكني is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and الله is the agent. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then there is no benefit for you and no advantage that returns to you". The wāw is a conjunction and من is conjoined to the yāʾ; معي is an adverb attached to the omitted ṣila of من; أو is a conjunction, and رحمنا is a past verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi. (فَمَنْ يُجِيرُ الْكافِرِينَ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ)
The fāʾ is causal; من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, i.e. no one, in the position of a nominative as an agent [Translator's note: so in the source, although it then makes يجير its khabar, which implies that من is a mubtadaʾ], and the clause يجير is the khabar; الكافرين is the object, and من عذاب أليم is attached to يجير. (قُلْ هُوَ الرَّحْمنُ آمَنَّا بِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنا) هو is a mubtadaʾ and الرحمن the khabar, and the clause آمنّا به is a second khabar; به is attached to آمنّا, عليه is attached to توكلنا, and the clause is conjoined to آمنّا به. (فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, the sīn is a particle of the future, and تعلمون is a verb and its agent; من is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and في ضلال مبين is the khabar of من. The interrogative clause stands in place of the two objects of تعلمون, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ ماؤُكُمْ غَوْراً فَمَنْ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِماءٍ مَعِينٍ) the parsing of أرأيتم came a short while ago, so refresh your acquaintance with it; the conditional clause stands in place of its two objects. ماؤكم is the subject of أصبح and غورا its khabar, i.e. sinking, going away into the channels of the earth, unreachable by buckets and ropes. The fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يأتيكم the khabar; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. بماء is attached to يأتيكم, and معين is an adjective of ماء, i.e. flowing on the surface, seen by the eyes. Its origin is معيون on the pattern مفعول, like مبيع whose origin is مبيوع: the ḍamma of the yāʾ was transferred to the ʿayn before it, so two sukūns met, the yāʾ and the wāw; the wāw was dropped, and then the ʿayn was given a kasra so that the yāʾ would remain sound. It is also said to be from معن الماء, i.e. the water was abundant; on this view it is faʿīl, not mafʿūl, and the mīm is a root letter, whereas on the first view the mīm is an augment, because the verb is عين.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «آمنّا به وعليه توكلنا» there is fronting and postponement: He fronted the object in His words وعليه توكلنا and postponed it in His words آمنّا به. Al-Zamakhsharī said on this:
«If you say: why did He postpone the object of آمنّا and front the object of توكلنا? I say: because آمنّا comes as an allusion (taʿrīḍ) to the disbelievers, since it occurs right after mentioning them, as if it were said: "We have believed and have not disbelieved as you disbelieved." Then He said وعليه توكلنا specifically: we have not relied on what you rely on — your men and your wealth.»
